key_insight: A two-stage, data-driven atomistic workflow can accurately model how amino-silane molecules passivate hybrid halide perovskite surfaces and how those interactions change with surface coverage.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical simulation framework for designing passivation strategies that reduce surface defects and improve perovskite solar-cell performance.
method: Curate a large open training set of diverse metal and hybrid halide perovskite structures (hyP-26).
Fine-tune the interatomic potential with a small, specialized dataset for an amino-silane passivating molecule.
Use the trained model to simulate mixed-composition perovskite surfaces across varying molecular coverages.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a multistep training pipeline validated through computational experiments on an experimentally realistic passivated perovskite surface system.
watch_item: Because the approach depends on carefully curated transfer learning and a narrow fine-tuning set, performance may be sensitive to coverage, chemistry, and surface configurations outside the training domain.
paper_title: Data-driven atomistic modelling of hybrid halide perovskite passivation
